headline: South African jurist who pursued war crimes wins the Nobel Peace Prize
headline_short: Navi Pillay wins the Nobel Peace Prize
deck: The 85-year-old once defended Nelson Mandela and chaired a UN inquiry that found Israel had committed genocide in Gaza.
standard: Navi Pillay, an 85-year-old South African human rights lawyer, won the Nobel Peace Prize on Friday. The Norwegian Nobel Committee credited her with ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted.

Under apartheid she defended Nelson Mandela, who became South Africa's first black president. She was later a judge at the UN's war crimes tribunal for Rwanda and the International Criminal Court, and the UN's high commissioner for human rights. She now sits on the International Court of Justice, the UN's principal court.
A UN commission she chaired concluded last year that Israel was committing genocide in Gaza. Israel condemned the award.
short: Navi Pillay, an 85-year-old South African human rights lawyer, won the Nobel Peace Prize on Friday for her work to see war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide prosecuted. A UN commission she chaired found last year that Israel was committing genocide in Gaza; Israel condemned the award.
